head: gc-quarantine-r3
report:
Too broad. Narrow to archive files.

NO DEFECTS

I found no defect in this change. I did not read all of the 15,507-line diff in the 20 minutes. I checked both findings from the earlier round in the code and with the author's tests. I also followed the new archive-resume path from each caller into `materializeSessionFile` and `restoreArchivedSessionLocked`.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier finding 1 (P2), "an unreadable quarantine directory still becomes 'No place holds a whole copy'": closed.**
- `readQuarantinePlace` (`session-archive.ts:1828-1868`) now looks up the record by name even when `readdir` fails.
  - In a place that can't be searched either (mode `0000`), `lstat` fails with EACCES. `readRegularText` reports that as unreadable, the place gets `copyUnreadable`, and the refusal says "could not be read … whether it is a whole copy … is not known".
  - In a place that can be searched but not listed (mode `0100`), the copy is read, and the refusal gives the copy-back step plus a "make … listable first" note (`listFirst`, lines 1942-1947).
- The "No place holds a whole copy" line (1953) is only reached when no place has a copy and no copy failed to read. With mode `0100` and nothing at the record's one quarantine name, that statement is true.
- Regression tests at `test/session-archive.test.ts:6148-6209` cover modes `0100`, `0000`, and `0000` beside a readable place that holds the copy, in both preview and apply. I ran them as uid 1000, so the permission checks were not skipped: `bun test test/session-archive.test.ts -t "does not say there is no copy|cannot read the archived transcript"` gave **7 pass, 0 fail, 91 expect() calls**.

**Earlier finding 2 (P2), "a bare catch turns a read failure into a false byte-difference diagnosis": closed.**
- `archivedHandleIsHeldBy` (`session-archive.ts:2557-2577`) no longer has `catch { return false; }`. A read error now propagates.
- Both reclaim callers wrap it in the new `compared()` (`gc-cli.ts:1160-1166`). It re-throws as "`<one>` could not be compared with `<other>`: `<error>`" instead of "holds what … does not". The callers are `proveEntryStillGoes` at 1808 and the archive-side caller at 1996.
- `openRegularFile` still returns undefined only for ENOENT. So "holds what … does not" now appears only when the target file is missing or the bytes really differ.
- As the earlier report asked, `publishedIsStaged` (lines 721-731) keeps its catch that returns false.

**Earlier report, the eight-failure sweep:** that was never a code finding, and its cause was left unproven. I could not rerun it here because repository-wide test runs are unavailable, so its status is unchanged.

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **The new `"archive"` scope value from `resolveResumableSession`.** I read every consumer: `main.ts` fork, `session-arg.ts`, `commands/share.ts`, `/pin` in `builtin-lifecycle.ts`, and `resolveResumeTarget`. None branches on `scope`; all of them read `session.path` or `session.id`. The `scope === "local"` test at `session-listing.ts:1018` is on a different local variable. Nothing drops the new value.
- **Using `bucketPath` in `findSessionContinuation` for a `.jsonl.gz` target.** The live bucket is searched for continuations, and both `target` and `bucketPath` go into `seen`, so neither the archive nor its live twin comes back as its own continuation.
- **`SessionManager.setSessionFile` now calls `materializeSessionFile` on every open.** When there is no archive beside the file, it returns the path after one `stat`. When there is an archive and no `.restoring` record, it returns the live path without taking leases. A caller's `loadedSession` snapshot is discarded only when the path came from the archive, and the comment there says why.
- **`restoreArchivedSessionLocked` when the live transcript already exists.** If the comparison fails, it throws naming the cause instead of reporting "different session". The record, leases and descriptor are released in `finally`.
- **Reading the legacy `settings.json` in `Settings`.** It runs only when `config.yml` is absent, and it is read-only. A missing file (ENOENT) is ignored without logging, and any other error is logged. It returns empty rather than throwing.
